newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PGA TV REVENUES TO DOUBLE BY 2000 -- COMMISSIONER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PGA TV REVENUES TO DOUBLE BY 2000 -- COMMISSIONER.

text.p: The average PGA Tour event will offer a purse of more than $3 million in 2000, according to tour commissioner Tim Finchem.

"Gross revenues from all television sources are expected to double," Finchem said Sunday as he announced television rights for tour events from 1999 through to 2002. The television revenues would then be an estimated $150 million, although tour officials would not release a figure.
"It would not be unreasonable to expect that by the year 2000 our official purses at PGA Tour events will average in excess of $3 million," said Finchem.

CBS network will continue to televise the most events, 67 over the four years covered by the new agreement. It will pick up the prestigious Memorial, and will also continue to cover the World Series of Golf, which will be revamped to become one of three new World Championship Series events.
ABC will cover 45 events, including the other two new World Championship Series events, one of which will be a matchplay event in February, the other a strokeplay tournament in November.
The World Championship Series, developed in response to calls for a World Tour, has been sanctioned by the five major international tours.
NBC will televise 24 events. It keeps the Players' Championship, and adds the Presidents Cup in 2000, 2002, 2004 and 2006.
Other tournaments will be covered on cable by ESPN, USA Network, the Golf Channel and Fox Sports.
Finchem said that for the first time, all four rounds of every official event would be televised.
"We'll have about a 20 percent increase in the number of hours on television, over 400 hours in 1999.
"Early-round coverage will be up significantly. Every one of our events will have Thursday, Friday coverage."
